what_it_does: System auditing — keeping a tamper-evident log of every sensitive action a computer takes (file opens, network connections, process launches) — is important for detecting intrusions, but it currently slows the monitored computer by more than 10% because the software that collects and forwards log entries must run on the very machine being watched, and protecting that software from tampering requires expensive OS mechanisms. DPUaudit moves log collection off the monitored machine entirely: a DPU (Data Processing Unit — a specialized network card with its own processor, physically separate from the host) reaches across the internal network link and pulls event records directly from the host's memory, the way a librarian retrieves books without the patron having to hand them over. Because the log-sender software no longer runs on the host, there is nothing on the host that needs heavy protection, and the overhead drops to near zero.
